one_liner: Multithreaded C cache server speaking RESP, memcache, HTTP and Postgres; about 2x Redis and 1.2-2.3x memcached throughput (author-run).
what_it_does: A standalone in-memory cache for string keys and values with TTLs, optional CAS, incr/decr, append/prepend, and sampled eviction at a memory limit. A single port auto-detects RESP2 (Redis/Valkey clients), the memcache text protocol, HTTP PUT/GET/DELETE and the Postgres wire protocol, so redis-cli, psql, curl and existing client libraries connect unchanged for the commands it supports. The core (src/pogocache.c + pogocache.h) can also be compiled into a C program as an in-process sharded cache with a callback-based store/load/delete/iter API.
how_it_is_fast: Keys are hashed with th64 (random seed per process) into one of 4096 shards by default. Each shard is an independent Robin Hood open-addressing table with 10-byte buckets (48-bit entry pointer, 24-bit hash fragment, 1-byte distance-to-bucket) guarded by its own compare-and-swap spinlock, so two threads rarely wait on the same lock. Each entry is one heap allocation (mimalloc by default) with keys packed at 6 bits per character ('sixpack'). Networking runs one epoll/kqueue loop per thread with connections assigned round-robin; each tick batches reads, command execution and writes, using io_uring to submit the batched reads/writes on Linux when enough sockets are ready, and low-memory eviction uses 2-random sampling instead of maintaining an LRU list.
when_to_use: Plain string GET/SET caching (sessions, rendered pages, query results; the benchmark used 1 B-1 KB values) where you want more ops per core than Redis or memcached and don't need Redis data types.

Request/response traffic with little or no pipelining (depth 1-10) from many connections. This is where the author's suite shows the largest margins: about 2x Redis at 8 threads, with GET p99 of 0.12 ms vs 0.21 ms for Redis.
CPU- or cost-limited hosts: about 7.1K CPU cycles per operation vs about 10K for Redis and 13.4K for memcached in the author's perf runs.
Replacing memcached for text-protocol clients when you also want TLS, a password, HTTP access and manual SAVE/LOAD snapshots in one binary on Linux or macOS.
An in-process cache in C/C++: drop in pogocache.c for a thread-safe sharded map with TTLs, eviction/notify callbacks and CAS, with no network hop.
when_not_to_use: You need Redis beyond strings. There are no hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, pub/sub, MULTI/EXEC, Lua, INFO/HELLO/CLIENT, or databases other than 0 (SELECT only accepts 0). Lists and other types are an open request (issue #14).

You need replication, failover or clustering. None exist, and high availability has been 'in the works' since Aug 2025 (issue #20). Persistence is only a manual SAVE/LOAD or a save on clean shutdown via --persist.
Deeply pipelined clients (depth 25-50). In the same suite Garnet beats it on GETs in 34 of 36 pipelined configurations, e.g. 29.5M vs 11.4M ops/s at 8 threads, pipeline 50.
Strict memory caps. The limit works by polling process RSS once a second. A third-party test with 1 MiB values on a Raspberry Pi 4 hit a VmHWM of 3.3 GB against --maxmemory 2 GiB (about 50% over).
Risk-averse production. It was first released in July 2025 by a single company/maintainer, and the only published throughput benchmark is the author's own.

integration.form: source-drop: the server binary is built with make (static release builds and a Docker image exist); pogocache.c + pogocache.h are embeddable
integration.dependencies: The server build git-clones and statically links mimalloc 3.1.5, jemalloc 5.3.0, liburing 2.12 (Linux) and OpenSSL 3.5.2, which needs cmake, autotools and perl at build time. Each can be disabled with NOMIMALLOC/NOJEMALLOC/NOURING/NOOPENSSL=1. The embedded pogocache.c needs only the C standard library.
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (stdatomic.h, static_assert) plus GCC/Clang extensions (__thread, __builtin_ia32_pause, -flto=auto); minimum compiler versions not documented
integration.platforms: 64-bit Linux and macOS (documented; CI on ubuntu-latest); x86-64 and aarch64 spin hints; benchmarked on ARM64 (AWS c8g); no Windows; the Makefile also has an Emscripten/WASM target
integration.thread_safety: Server: one event loop per thread (default = core count). Embedded API: safe for concurrent use through per-shard spinlocks. Waiters busy-spin unless you supply a yield callback, and the usethreadbatch mode is non-reentrant.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it speaks the memcache text protocol (no meta or binary protocol; CAS is off unless --cas yes) and a RESP2 subset of Redis covering strings and TTLs. It listens on 127.0.0.1:9401 by default and has no Redis data structures, scripting, transactions, pub/sub or replication.

gotchas: CAS is disabled by default (--cas no). Memcache `gets` returns CAS 0 and every `cas` fails until the server is started with --cas yes.
Hash buckets store 48-bit pointers. The build assumes heap addresses fit in 48 bits; compile with NO48BITPTRS to get 8-byte pointers on systems with larger virtual address spaces or tagged pointers.

Embedded mode: the hash seed defaults to 0 (only the server picks a random seed), and there is no built-in memory limit; eviction happens only when the caller passes lowmem=true on store. The header comment says the default is 65536 shards, but the code uses 4096.
It binds to loopback by default, so in Docker or Kubernetes you must pass -h 0.0.0.0 or clients get dropped connections (issue #21). The --auth password can only be given on the command line.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Pogocache over Dragonfly when clients mostly GET/SET strings at low pipeline depth and CPU per request matters: it beat Dragonfly in every thread/pipeline cell of the author's suite, by 1.1x to 5x. Pick Garnet instead for heavily pipelined clients, and Dragonfly when you need broader Redis command coverage. The embedded pogocache.c plays the in-process role for C that Caffeine plays on the JVM.
verified_claims_summary: The only benchmark is the author's cache-benchmarks suite: memtier_benchmark with 256 connections over a local UNIX socket, 1-1024 B values, persistence off, server pinned to 16 cores of an AWS c8g.8xlarge (ARM64), median of 31 runs. At 8 threads and pipeline 1, Pogocache 1.2.0 did 3.08M GET/s and 2.95M SET/s vs 1.51M/1.67M for Redis 8.2.1 and 2.60M/1.27M for memcached 1.6.38, with GET p99 of 0.119 ms vs 0.207 ms and 0.191 ms. It beats Redis, Valkey, memcached and Dragonfly in every thread/pipeline cell (smallest margin: 1.07x over memcached on GET at 1 thread, pipeline 10). No compiler flags are stated, and the older README table (about 3.5x Redis) is stale.
